comments.text: The part that stuck with me: almost every river border on Earth runs down the middle of the water, but the 1890 line between Namibia and South Africa was put on the northern bank. So the Orange River sits entirely inside South Africa, and Namibia's territory stops at the waterline. Namibia asked for a midstream line after independence in 1990, and the talks are still unresolved. Sources are listed in the description. Does a river, lake or canal decide a border where you live, and does anyone argue about who owns the water?
